questions.q: What does research link living in a cluttered home to?
a: Higher levels of the stress hormone cortisol
Lower sensitivity to everyday noise
Faster recovery from a lack of sleep
Stronger immune system responses
questions.why: Lesson 1 says cortisol is higher in cluttered homes, raising the risk of anxiety and depression.

questions.q: What small daily habit does the summary suggest to begin decluttering?
a: Making your bed each morning
Clearing one cupboard shelf
Throwing out one item per hour
Cleaning the kitchen before bed
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends one little win, starting with making the bed each day.

questions.q: Which items does the summary say you should keep when sorting a room?
a: Only things you use about once a month or more
Anything that still works properly
Everything with sentimental value
Items you might need some day
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to keep only what you use at most once a month and to throw things away ruthlessly.

questions.q: Why does the summary call the bedroom one of the most important rooms to declutter?
a: Clutter there makes it hard to sleep well
Guests see it more often than other rooms
It usually holds the most valuable items
It is the easiest room to clean quickly
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a cluttered bedroom distracts you at bedtime and should become a sleep sanctuary.

questions.q: What is the problem with many common cleaning products, according to the summary?
a: They release harmful gases called VOCs
They leave a sticky film on surfaces
They cost far more than natural options
They stop working after a few months
questions.why: Lesson 3 says volatile organic compounds pollute indoor air and can harm children.
